detail.body:
Fixes #8475.

(Originally opened against #8469, which @gss10282023 withdrew and resubmitted as #8475 while this was being written. The discussion about how this and #8476 relate is on #8469 and continues on #8475.)

## The measurement

`clip_grad_norm_` ends by averaging the per-rank norms over the data parallel group:

```python
pg = groups._get_data_parallel_group()
scaled_norm = total_norm * 1.0 / float(dist.get_world_size(group=pg))
dist.all_reduce(scaled_norm_tensor, group=pg)
```

That reconstructs a global norm only while every rank holds the same parameters. Expert parameters are not replicated, so each rank's norm describes a different set of experts. Four expert gradients across two ranks, measured on 2×H20:

| layout | global norm |
| --- | ---: |
| reference — each expert counted once | **10.954452** (`sqrt(120)`) |
| replicated on both ranks | 10.954452 |
| one half per rank | **7.236068** |

`sqrt(20)` and `sqrt(100)` averaged to 7.236 instead of `sqrt(20 + 100)`. The same gradients, 34% apart, decided only by where the experts happen to live. `clip_coef` is `max_norm / total_norm`, so wherever clipping is active this changes the update.

@gss10282023 reported this (#8475) and measured a 0.2 shift in the clipping coefficient on their setup; the numbers above are an independent reproduction from a different direction.

## Why the fix is the repo's own

`get_norm_with_moe_layers` already does it correctly — it takes the non-expert norm plus the expert gradients keyed by group, reduces each expert group over its own `moe_ep_group`, and combines as `(Σ norm_i ** p) ** (1/p)`. **Both the bf16 and the fp16 optimizer already call it.**

The fp32 path instead inlines the approximation. That approximation also exists under its own name, `get_norm_with_moe_layers_fast`, carrying this comment:

> This implementation standardizes the grad_norm across ranks. A more precise implementation can be found in 'get_norm_with_moe_layers'.

and that named copy has **no callers at all** — so the warning never reaches the one place still doing it. This PR keeps expert gradients out of the replicated norm and folds them in through the precise helper, leaving fp32 the same shape as the other two optimizers.

## Scope

**Unchanged when no expert parameter is present** — that branch is the original code, not touched. Every non-MoE fp32 run behaves exactly as before, which the existing suite confirms (below).

Two guards worth naming:

- An expert parameter carrying no `group_name` has no expert parallel group to reduce over. `TestClipGradNorm::test_gather` builds one by hand exactly like that, so such a call stays on the original path rather than guessing a group.
- `get_norm_with_moe_layers` reports a non-finite norm as `-1`. Used as-is that would make `clip_coef` negative and flip the sign of every gradient, so it is mapped to `inf` — which keeps what the averaging path already did, scale to zero.

## Testing

`tests/unit/runtime/test_runtime_utils.py`, 2 GPUs (H20): 16 passed.

The cases that call `clip_grad_norm_` directly assert the **norm value**, not that a code path was reached, and cover experts spread over ranks, a rank whose experts got no tokens, a rank owning no expert, a rank with no gradient at all, the expert-only inf norm, and the order the expert groups are visited in.

`TestClipFp32GradientsThroughEngine` goes through `deepspeed.initialize`, `backward` and `step` in an fp32 run without ZeRO, with one expert on each of two ranks and a dense layer in front. The engine drops the norm `clip_grad_norm_` returns, so the test reads it from its effect: with plain SGD the update is `lr * clip_coef * grad`, so it computes the global norm independently from the gradients (each dense gradient once, each rank's expert once) and checks every parameter after `step()` against `start - lr * clip_coef * grad`. It also checks that the clip is active and that the average of the ranks' own norms, the old answer, differs from the true one by more than 5%, so it cannot pass by accident. On this setup the true norm is 0.624 and the average is 0.542.

```
this branch                         16 passed
branch's test file on the code      TestClipFp32GradientsThroughEngine fails:
before this PR                          AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
                                        Greatest absolute difference: 3.2e-05 (up to 1e-06 allowed)
```

It uses the plain `MoE` layer, not AutoEP: the code under test reads `is_moe_param` and `group_name` and reduces over the expert parallel group, which both paths share.

Earlier, on the first revision, `test_runtime_utils.py` + `tests/unit/v1/moe/test_moe.py` compared by failure set on the same box:

```
master   7 failed, 29 passed, 14 skipped
branch   6 failed, 30 passed, 14 skipped

only failing on branch (regressions) -> none
only failing on master               -> test_sharded_experts_count_once   (the new one)
failing on both                      -> 6
```

The 6 were pre-existing there, `ImportError: libcudart.so.13`, unrelated to this change. I have not rerun `test_moe.py` since the later commits.

## Note

#8470 proposed a fix for the same issue and was closed by its author without discussion. This takes a different route: rather than repairing the averaging, it routes the fp32 path through the combiner the other two optimizers already use, so there is one implementation of the correct thing instead of two.


## Environment

NVIDIA H20-3e, driver 580.105.08, Python 3.11.15, torch 2.9.1+cu128; the runs above used 2 GPUs.

+        expert_tensors = {group_name: [] for group_name in expert_group_names}

-        total_norm = torch.stack(all_norms).max()

@@ -421,14 +482,26 @@ def clip_grad_norm_(parameters, max_norm, norm_type=2, mpu=None):

+    def test_sharded_experts_count_once(self):
+        """The global norm must not depend on how experts are spread over ranks.
+
+        Rank-averaging the per-rank norms only reconstructs a global norm when every
+        rank holds the same parameters. Under expert parallelism they do not, so the
+        four experts below gave sqrt(20) and sqrt(100) averaged to 7.236 instead of
+        the sqrt(120) = 10.954 that counting each expert once produces (#8469).
+        """
+        groups._create_expert_and_data_parallel(2)
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        device = get_accelerator().device_name(rank)
+
+        experts = [torch.full((4, ), float(v)) for v in (1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0)]
+        expected = torch.cat(experts).norm(2).item()
+
+        owned = experts[:2] if rank == 0 else experts[2:]
+        params = []
+        for grad in owned:
+            param = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(4, device=device))
+            param.grad = grad.clone().to(device)
+            param.allreduce = False
+            param.group_name = "ep_size_2"
+            params.append(param)
+
+        # A max_norm far above the norm leaves the gradients alone, so this reads the
+        # computed norm rather than the clipped result.
+        norm = ds_utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, max_norm=1e9)

+        assert abs(float(norm) -

+
+    def _expert(self, value, device, with_grad=True):
+        param = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(4, device=device))
+        if with_grad:
+            param.grad = torch.full((4, ), value, device=device)
+        param.allreduce = False
+        param.group_name = "ep_size_2"
+        return param
+
+    def _plain(self, value, device):
+        param = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(4, device=device))
+        param.grad = torch.full((4, ), value, device=device)

+
+    def test_experts_idle_on_one_rank_do_not_deadlock(self):
+        """A rank whose experts got no tokens must take the same collectives (#8469).
+
+        Ownership has to be read from the parameters, not the gradients: `p.grad is
+        not None` filtering drops an unused expert, and branching on what is left made
+        one rank reduce over the expert group while its peer reduced over the data
+        parallel group. They then waited on each other.
+        """
+        groups._create_expert_and_data_parallel(2)
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        device = get_accelerator().device_name(rank)
+
+        expert = self._expert(2.0, device, with_grad=(rank == 0))
+        norm = ds_utils.clip_grad_norm_([self._plain(1.0, device), expert], max_norm=1e9)

+        # non-expert 2.0 replicated, one expert of norm 4.0 owned by rank 0:
+        # sqrt(2**2 + 4**2).
+        assert abs(float(norm) - 20**0.5) < 1e-4
+
+    def test_a_rank_owning_no_expert_does_not_deadlock(self):
+        """Under pipeline parallelism a rank can hold no expert at all.
+
+        Local ownership then differs in kind rather than in degree, so the branch is
+        settled by one all-reduced flag instead of by what this rank happens to hold.
+        """
+        groups._create_expert_and_data_parallel(2)
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        device = get_accelerator().device_name(rank)
+
+        params = [self._plain(1.0, device)]
+        if rank == 0:
+            params.append(self._expert(2.0, device))
+
+        norm = ds_utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, max_norm=1e9)
+        assert abs(float(norm) - 20**0.5) < 1e-4
+
+    def test_expert_only_inf_norm(self):
+        """Nothing replicated leaves no tensor to take a max over; zero is the identity."""
+        groups._create_expert_and_data_parallel(2)
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        device = get_accelerator().device_name(rank)

+        norm = ds_utils.clip_grad_norm_([self._expert(float(rank + 1), device)], max_norm=1e9, norm_type=float('inf'))

+        assert abs(float(norm) - 2.0) < 1e-4

+        """Every local gradient can be absent, expert ones included, and the rank still has to answer."""
+        groups._create_expert_and_data_parallel(2)
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        device = get_accelerator().device_name(rank)

+        norm = ds_utils.clip_grad_norm_([self._expert(2.0, device, with_grad=(rank == 1))], max_norm=1e9)

+class _OneMoELayer(torch.nn.Module):
+    """A dense layer, then one expert per rank behind a gate."""
+
+    def __init__(self, hidden_dim):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.dense = torch.nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
+        expert = torch.nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
+        # k=2 sends every token to both experts, so each rank's expert gets a gradient.
+        self.moe = MoE(hidden_size=hidden_dim, expert=expert, num_experts=2, ep_size=2, k=2, capacity_factor=2.0)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        output, _, _ = self.moe(self.dense(x))
+        return output.pow(2).mean()
+
+
+class TestClipFp32GradientsThroughEngine(DistributedTest):
+    """The clip `DeepSpeedEngine.step()` applies in an fp32 run without ZeRO, with experts on two ranks.
+
+    `clip_grad_norm_` returns its norm and the engine drops it, so the norm is read from its effect. With
+    plain SGD the update is `lr * clip_coef * grad`, and the coefficient has to come from the norm of every
+    gradient with each expert counted once, not from the ranks' own norms averaged.
+    """
+
+    world_size = 2
+
+    def test_the_update_is_clipped_by_the_global_norm(self):
+        hidden_dim, max_norm, lr = 8, 1e-3, 1.0
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        model = _OneMoELayer(hidden_dim)
+        param_group = {'params': list(model.parameters()), 'name': 'all'}
+        optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(split_params_into_different_moe_groups_for_optimizer(param_group), lr=lr)
+        config = {
+            "train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 2,
+            "gradient_clipping": max_norm,
+            "zero_optimization": {
+                "stage": 0
+            }
+        }
+        engine, _, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(config=config, model=model, optimizer=optimizer)
+
+        # A different loss scale on each rank gives the two experts gradients of different size.
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(100 + rank)
+        x = torch.randn(2, 4, hidden_dim, generator=generator).to(engine.device)
+        engine.backward(engine(x) * (1 + 3 * rank))
+
+        params = list(engine.module.parameters())
+        dense = [p for p in params if not is_moe_param(p)]
+        experts = [p for p in params if is_moe_param(p)]
+        assert dense and experts
+        dense_sq = torch.stack([p.grad.float().pow(2).sum() for p in dense]).sum()
+        expert_sq = torch.stack([p.grad.float().pow(2).sum() for p in experts]).sum()
+
+        # The oracle counts a dense gradient once because it is the same on both ranks, and an expert once
+        # because each rank owns a different one.
+        dense_on_every_rank = dense_sq.clone()
+        dist.all_reduce(dense_on_every_rank, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN)
+        assert torch.equal(dense_on_every_rank, dense_sq), "dense gradients should match across ranks"
+        all_experts_sq = expert_sq.clone()
+        dist.all_reduce(all_experts_sq)
+        true_norm = (dense_sq + all_experts_sq).sqrt().item()
+
+        # Averaging the ranks' own norms is the answer this test exists to rule out, so it has to differ.
+        own_norm = (dense_sq + expert_sq).sqrt()
+        dist.all_reduce(own_norm)
+        averaged_norm = own_norm.item() / dist.get_world_size()
+        assert true_norm > 5 * max_norm, "the clip must be active for this to say anything"
+        assert abs(averaged_norm - true_norm) > 0.05 * true_norm, "the two norms must be distinguishable"
+
+        clip_coef = max_norm / (true_norm + 1e-6)
+        before = [p.detach().clone() for p in params]
+        grads = [p.grad.detach().clone() for p in params]
+        engine.step()
+
+        for p, start, grad in zip(params, before, grads):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(p.detach(), start - lr * clip_coef * grad, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-6)
+
+
 class TestClipGradNormPNorm(DistributedTest):
     # world_size 1 so this runs wherever the suite runs; the bug is in the per-rank
     # recombination of the norms, which is independent of the group size.

inline_comments.body:
I read this against 338ed51 rather than running it, so this is a question about the branch selector, not a repro.

Your comment above says the all-reduced flag is what settles the pipeline-parallel case, where a rank owns no expert parameter at all. The flag is reduced over `groups._get_data_parallel_group()`, and under pipeline parallelism that group does not span stages:

- `deepspeed/__init__.py:258` passes `model.mpu()` for a `PipelineModule`, which is the `PipelineParallelGrid` (`runtime/pipe/module.py:566`)
- `runtime/engine.py:2048` copies it into `groups.mpu`
- `utils/groups.py:707-711` then returns `mpu.get_data_parallel_group()`
- `runtime/pipe/topology.py:436` documents that as "The group of ranks within the same stage of all pipelines"

So each stage votes among itself. If experts sit on some stages and not others, two stages can reach different `expert_group_names` and issue different collectives, which is the divergence the vote is there to prevent. Your harness is 2 ranks with no pipe dimension, so it would not show this either way. Is `_clone_world_group()` what you want here, or does something already keep MoE inside a single stage?

One smaller thing on the same lines. `clip_grad_norm_` is a per-step call from `_take_model_step`, so the vote costs an all-reduce and two `.item()` syncs on every fp32 clip. With no MoE configured `_EXPERT_PARALLEL_GROUP` is empty and `sorted(... or {})` gives `[]` whichever way the vote goes, so reading the registry locally first would skip it, on the same "built identically on every rank" argument you use two lines down.

issue_comments.body:
**Do not review this as it stands — two defects found by @gss10282023 on #8469, both of which I reproduced.**

1. **Collective deadlock** when one rank holds no expert gradient. I branch on whether *this rank* has expert gradients and the two branches issue different collectives, so a rank whose experts got no tokens this step waits on a peer that took the other path. `p.grad is not None` filtering makes that ordinary in MoE training, not a corner case.

2. **Exception** on expert-only `norm_type=inf`: `norm_parameters` is empty and `torch.stack([])` raises.

Marking this as a draft while I fix both. The branch decision has to be rank-independent — `_EXPERT_PARALLEL_GROUP` is built identically everywhere, so iterating its group names and contributing a zero tensor where this rank holds nothing keeps the collectives symmetric no matter which experts got tokens.

There is also #8476 from @gss10282023 covering the AutoEP FP32 L2 path. We are discussing on #8469 whether these should be one change; if a maintainer prefers a single PR, theirs came first.

@gss10282023 Both fixed in `338ed51`, and both reproduced on 2×H20 before I touched anything.

**Deadlock.** Your diagnosis was exactly right, and your own patch already had the answer in a comment I should have read more carefully:

> Inspect ownership before filtering gradients: an unused expert on one rank must not make that rank choose a different collective from the others.

I was reading ownership *after* `p.grad is not None` filtering. Ownership now comes from the parameters.

That alone was not enough, though — your case was "no expert **gradients**", and there is a harder one: a rank owning no expert **parameter** at all, which happens under pipeline parallelism. Local inspection cannot settle that in kind, so the choice is now made by one all-reduced flag, with group names taken from `_EXPERT_PARALLEL_GROUP` (built identically on every rank). A rank holding nothing for a group contributes a zero, which adds nothing to a sum of p-th powers and nothing to a max of absolute values.

Measured, same harness that hung before:

```
uneven  (rank1 owns no expert at all)     both ranks return 4.4721
nograd  (rank1's expert got no tokens)    both ranks return 4.4721
inf     (expert-only, norm_type=inf)      both ranks return 2.0000
```

`sqrt(2**2 + 4**2)` — the non-expert 2.0 replicated, plus one expert of norm 4.0 owned by rank 0. The original sharded-expert number is unchanged at 10.954452.

**Expert-only inf norm** was `torch.stack([])` with nothing replicated left to take a max over; zero is the identity there.

Three tests added for your cases. On `master`, run individually, all four fail with `AssertionError` — no hangs, since master has no expert branch to diverge on. (Run together they cascade into `TimeoutError`: a failed assertion in one rank of a `DistributedTest` leaves the other waiting. Worth knowing if you see that in your own runs.)

On the split: having read #8476, I do not think either subsumes the other. Yours keys on `ds_zero_placement_family == "autoep_expert"` with its own `ds_autoep_ep_size`, `norm_type == 2` and `mpu is None`; mine keys on `is_moe_param`/`group_name` and routes through `get_norm_with_moe_layers` for every norm type. Different families, different coverage.

What I would rather not do is leave `clip_grad_norm_` with two special cases bolted on. If AutoEP experts can be given a `group_name` and an entry in `_EXPERT_PARALLEL_GROUP`, the helper route covers both and the ownership weighting falls out of the group size — but you know the AutoEP placement model far better than I do, so tell me whether that holds. If it does not, I will take yours as the shape and fold legacy MoE into it.

Un-drafting since the two defects are closed, but I am in no hurry for this to land ahead of that conversation.

@tohtana @sfc-gh-truwase Could one of you take a look when you have time? The branch merges cleanly with master. @ebarkhordar reviewed both revisions and ran the cases (thread above): the per-step cost is back to master's, and the pipeline-parallel vote now reduces over the world group.

With MoE and fp32 gradient clipping, expert gradients were counted twice in the global norm, so clipping triggered early and scaled every update too small.

Thanks. I only see the three Copilot comments on this PR, no codex ones, so let me know if I missed something. The expert group order and the result device are fixed, and I added an engine-level test: backward and step on 2 GPUs, checked against a global norm computed separately. 16 passed on 2 H20s.
